summary: A get must let the woman marry anyone. If the husband says "except so-and-so," the Sages say it does not work, and the mishnah tells how to fix it.

chunks.st: man except [ella] for so-and-so,

summary: If a husband says his wife may marry anyone except people she could never marry anyway, the get is good. But if he leaves out someone she could marry, it is not.

chunks.en: "You may marry any
chunks.st: If a man says to his wife while handing her a bill of divorce: You are hereby permitted to marry any

chunks.st: man, except to marry my father or to marry your father,

chunks.en: my brother or your brother,
chunks.st: to marry my brother or to marry your brother,

chunks.en: a slave or a non-Jew,
chunks.st: to marry a slave or to marry a gentile,

chunks.st: except for when doing so violates the following: The prohibition against a widow being married to a High Priest;

chunks.en: a divorced woman or a chalutzah to a regular Kohen,

summary: Three kinds of get are not proper, but if a woman married with one of them, her child is still kosher. Rabbi Elazar says a get given in front of witnesses works even with no signatures.

chunks.en: Three kinds of get are not valid,
chunks.st: Three bills of divorce are invalid ab initio,

chunks.en: but if she married,
chunks.st: but if the woman marries another man
chunks.stMore: on the basis of one of these bills of divorce

chunks.en: the child is kosher.
chunks.st: the lineage of the offspring from this marriage is unflawed.
chunks.stMore: In other words, she is not considered to be a married woman who engaged in sexual intercourse with another man, which would impair the lineage of their child. These three bills are:

chunks.he: כָּתַב בִּכְתַב יָדוֹ וְאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים,

chunks.st: a case where there are signatures of witnesses on the document but there is no date written on it,

chunks.en: or it has a date but it has
chunks.st: and a case where there is a date written on it, but it contains

chunks.st: only one witness.

chunks.en: these are the three gittin that are not valid.
chunks.st: These are the three invalid bills of divorce

chunks.en: But if she married,
chunks.st: with regard to which the Sages said: And if she marries,

chunks.en: the child is kosher.
chunks.st: the lineage of the offspring is unflawed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים
chunks.en: even if there are no witnesses on it,
chunks.st: Even though there are no signatures of witnesses on the document,

chunks.en: but he gave it to her in front of witnesses,
chunks.st: but he handed it to her in the presence of two witnesses,

chunks.en: it is valid, and she can collect even from sold property,
chunks.st: it is a valid bill of divorce. And on the basis of this bill of divorce the woman can collect the amount written for her in her marriage contract even from liened property, as Rabbi Eliezer maintains that

chunks.en: because the witnesses sign the get
chunks.st: the witnesses sign the bill of divorce

chunks.en: only to make the world better.
chunks.st: only for the betterment of the world.
chunks.stMore: If no witnesses sign a bill of divorce the husband can contest its validity at any time by denying that he wrote it. Nevertheless, the witnesses’ signatures are not an essential part of a bill of divorce.

summary: When two gittin get mixed up, both must be given to each wife. When several gittin are written on one page, the witnesses' signatures decide which ones are valid.

chunks.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁשָּׁלְחוּ שְׁנֵי גִטִּין שָׁוִין וְנִתְעָרְבוּ,
chunks.en: Two men who sent two gittin that were the same, and they got mixed up,
chunks.st: With regard to a case of two men who sent their wives two identical bills of divorce with an agent, as both their names and their wives’ names are identical, and the two bills of divorce were mixed up,

chunks.en: he gives both to this wife and both to that wife.
chunks.st: the agent should hand both bills of divorce to this wife and both of them to that wife, so that each wife definitely receives her bill of divorce, although it is unclear which one is hers.

chunks.en: So, if one of them got lost,
chunks.st: Therefore, if one of the bills of divorce was lost before it was given to both women,

chunks.en: the other one is cancelled.
chunks.st: the other is void,
chunks.stMore: because it is unknown which bill of divorce was meant for which woman.

chunks.en: Five men who wrote one shared text in the get,
chunks.st: With regard to five husbands who wrote a general wording in the bill of divorce,
chunks.stMore: i.e., who wrote one common bill of divorce for their wives with a single formula, writing that

chunks.he: אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי מְגָרֵשׁ פְּלוֹנִית וּפְלוֹנִי פְּלוֹנִית,
chunks.en: "The man so-and-so divorces so-and-so, and so-and-so divorces so-and-so,"

chunks.en: and it must be given to each one.

chunks.st: and the witnesses signed below,

chunks.en: the one the witnesses are read with is valid.
chunks.st: the formula with which the witnesses’ signatures are read is valid. In other words, the formula directly underneath which they signed is valid, and the others are not valid.

chunks.en: is valid. If the top of this one is next to

summary: A get is valid even if written in one language and signed in another, and even if the witnesses sign in different ways. A get the husband was forced to give is valid only if a Jewish beis din made him.

chunks.en: A get written in Hebrew with its witnesses in Greek,
chunks.st: With regard to a bill of divorce that was written in Hebrew and its witnesses signed in Greek,

chunks.en: or in Greek with its witnesses in Hebrew,

summary: If everyone in town says a woman is engaged or divorced, we believe it, unless there is another way to explain the talk.

chunks.en: If word went around the city that she is engaged,
chunks.st: If a rumor circulated in the city that an unmarried woman is betrothed,

chunks.en: she is engaged.
chunks.st: she is considered to be betrothed.

chunks.en: Divorced, she is divorced,
chunks.st: Similarly, if a rumor circulated that a married woman is divorced, she is divorced,

chunks.en: as long as there is no other explanation.
chunks.st: provided there is no valid alternative explanation [amatla] for the rumor.

chunks.en: What is an explanation?
chunks.st: What is considered a valid explanation?

chunks.en: "So-and-so divorced
chunks.st: For example, it is a case where there is a rumor that so-and-so divorced

chunks.en: his wife with a condition,"
chunks.st: his wife but that the bill of divorce was given to her conditionally.
chunks.stMore: It is therefore possible that the condition was not fulfilled and she is not actually divorced.

chunks.en: "he threw her kiddushin to her,
chunks.st: Similarly, if there is a rumor that a woman was betrothed but that the man threw her betrothal, i.e., the money or document of betrothal, to her,

chunks.he: סָפֵק קָרוֹב לָהּ סָפֵק קָרוֹב לוֹ,
chunks.en: maybe closer to her, maybe closer to him,"
chunks.st: and it is uncertain whether it was closer to her and uncertain whether it was closer to him,
chunks.stMore: and therefore the status of their betrothal is likewise uncertain,

chunks.en: this is an explanation.
chunks.st: this is considered a valid explanation.

summary: Beis Shammai, Beis Hillel, and Rabbi Akiva argue about what reasons let a man divorce his wife, and each learns it from a pasuk.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.st: A man may not divorce his wife unless

chunks.en: he found in her something not modest,
chunks.st: he finds out about her having engaged in a matter of forbidden sexual intercourse [devar erva],
chunks.stMore: i.e., she committed adultery or is suspected of doing so,

chunks.en: as it says in Devarim,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Because he found in her something not proper."
chunks.st: “Because he has found some unseemly matter [ervat davar] in her, and he writes her a scroll of severance” (Deuteronomy 24:1).

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: even if she burned his food,
chunks.st: He may divorce her even due to a minor issue, e.g., because she burned or over-salted his dish,

chunks.en: as it says there,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Because he found in her something not proper."
chunks.st: “Because he has found some unseemly matter in her,” meaning that he found any type of shortcoming in her.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: even if he found another woman nicer looking than her,
chunks.st: He may divorce her even if he found another woman who is better looking than her and wishes to marry her,

chunks.en: as it says there,
chunks.st: as it is stated in that verse:

chunks.he: וְהָיָה אִם לֹא תִמְצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָיו:
chunks.en: "And if she does not find favor in his eyes."
chunks.st: “And it comes to pass, if she finds no favor in his eyes” (Deuteronomy 24:1).
